_what: A recommended local title for every Subjects row with no catalog heading, and a recommended common subject code for every credit row with none, each with the 0-100 confidence its source measured (Sam on #3655, 2026-11-21). A recommendation is for a person to accept or change; nothing reads it as a title or a mapping. A row whose courses are all noncredit is lined up with the standing noncredit subject title list by its dominant COCI noncredit category. Built by kb/_build_local_subject_recommendations.py; no clock is read.
_confidence: A whole number from 0 to 100 (Sam, 2026-11-25: confidence bars 0-100 rather than low, med, high): the share of the titled codes, each left out of its own vote, for which the source's condition gave the catalog's own heading. A condition asked fewer than 20 codes scores 59 at most; program titles 89 at most. Sources that agree join at 100 x (1 - the product of (1 - score / 100)), 99 at most; where another source differs, it is listed under also and every candidate scores 89 at most. Totals count recommendations by band: 90_plus, 60_to_89, under_60.

noncredit.note: Measured on the noncredit-only codes that hold a catalog heading (titles) or a common code from the subject map (codes), each left out of its own vote. A title condition right less than half the time is a guess: it stays measured here, used false, and gives no recommendation. The common code's answer key is the subject map, which reads a code without its credit or noncredit band (f-subject-map-ignores-credit-band-s698), so its share is a floor.
